newsitem.title: LEBANON: Christie's launches bid for Middle East art market.
newsitem.headline: Christie's launches bid for Middle East art market.

text.p: Christie's international auction house exhibited a selection of its wares in Lebanon on Friday as a first step towards developing a role in the Middle East art market.
In a bid to tempt Lebanese buyers, it showed a selection of rugs, carpets and 19th century paintings that will be auctioned shortly in London.
The two-day exhibition at a hotel in the mountains overlooking the Lebanese capital is the first Christie's have staged in the Middle East.
"We are trying to encourage people who are a little bit timid who would like to buy western art," Lord Paltimore, Christie's expert in 19th century art, told a news conference.
The London-based company is the world's biggest fine arts auctioneer with an annual turnover of $1 billion.
Dermot Chichester, director responsible for development in the Middle East, said Christie's was examining the size of the regional art market and the possibility of making Beirut its regional centre.

"I think by focusing on Lebanon we can then extend our tentacles into other countries in the Middle East," Chichester said. "But realistically it is not going to be possible to hold auction sales here in anything less than two years."
